FIX ROUND 429s11 for issue #429, DECISION 0050 RULING 7: EACH AGGREGATE EMITS WHAT IT CAN RETURN, AND A REVIEW PANEL'S DECLARED WORDS STILL END THE SEQUENCE. The branch is story-429-sequence-endings, checked out in this worktree at 6c0914dd7 (ten commits on main f0e0c9645; 6c0914dd7 is fix round 429s10). When you are done, the branch is 6c0914dd7 plus your commits. Do not rebase, squash, amend or merge main: the controller restacks.

WHERE IT STANDS:
- Fix round 429s10 (fix-round-429s10-for-issue-429-d-a65e43ec) built `Aggregate::emits` as the one home read by `endings` and `refuse_unreachable`, with both commissioned cases passing by name:
  - `crucible_review_sequence::a_final_panel_that_cannot_emit_refuse_lets_an_earlier_refuse_end_the_sequence` (step=first, why=ends-on, REVIEW-REFUSE, AwaitingOperator);
  - `bundle::sequence_tests::a_table_arm_no_reachable_step_or_aggregate_can_emit_is_refused` (REVIEW-GHOST, with a reachable control).
  The storage test pins `EngineError::Store(StoreError::Sqlite(_))`. Keep all of it.
- Its chief stopped it at REVIEW-SECURITY-HOLD, high, recorded on #429 (https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/429#issuecomment-6545990609).

THE OPERATOR'S RULING: 2026-10-31, in chat, "go with recommended" (#429, https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/429#issuecomment-6548911517): fix round 429s11 as below; review_panel's handling of an out-of-vocabulary member word is NOT changed in this round (follow-up ask (g)).

THE FINDING (fix it; write the case as a named test, failing before your fix):
**HIGH, security (decision 0050 ruling 7; decision 0071 ruling 5): the narrowing drops a declared hard word from a non-final review-panel step, so the engine no longer stops on it.**
- (i) `parse_panel` (bundle/parse.rs about :277) only requires a panel step's declared results to cover `Aggregate::required_results`, so a review-panel step may declare a superset such as `hold`.
- (ii) `review_panel` (bundle/aggregate.rs about :142-147) returns the worst member word verbatim, so a member reporting a declared `hold` makes the step's result `hold`.
- (iii) A non-final step's only vocabulary check, `vocabulary_problem` (engine/sequence.rs about :756), admits any word in `step.results`.
- (iv) `emittable` (bundle/sequence.rs about :431) narrows a panel's words to `emits()`, so `stamp_sequence` compiles `ends_on` and `hard_results` to [security-hold] only.
- (v) `ends_sequence` (engine/sequence.rs about :167) reads those sets, the step checkpoints, and the final `clean` completes the run.
- Case `a_review_panel_step_ends_on_a_declared_hard_word_beyond_its_required_results`:
  - a v2 table: work/complete → review; review/clean → done; review/residual parks; review/security-hold and review/hold → a terminal stop, both hard;
  - the seat declares [clean, residual, security-hold, hold];
  - the first step is a review-panel declaring the same four, and both members report `hold`;
  - the final step is a single step reporting `clean`.
  - Expected: `first.ends_on` and `hard_results` contain `hold`; `effect/succeeded` carries result=hold, step=first, why=hard-word; the run is Stopped. Observed at 6c0914dd7: both sets are [security-hold], `hold` checkpoints, and the final `clean` completes the run (Completed, not Stopped). At base 1ce89ddf5 the run stopped.

THE FIX (recommended, within this round's limits: no change to what an aggregate computes, no change to `parse_panel`):
- `emits` answers per aggregate, by an explicit match (no wildcard): `unanimous-pass` emits exactly [pass, fail], which is all `unanimous_pass` can return for valid members; `review-panel` emits the step's DECLARED results, because `review_panel` returns a member's declared word verbatim. It takes the step's declared results as its input where it needs them.
- `required_results` stays the cover set `parse_panel` checks.
- So a review-panel step's `ends_on`/`hard_results` equal the base's (every declared word), and both chief cases, which are unanimous-pass, still hold.
- `emits`' doc says what each aggregate returns. The claim that review-panel's unknown member word is parked by `decide()` is true only for an undeclared word; at a non-final step an undeclared word is failed by `vocabulary_problem` (a failed attempt, 0006-retryable). State exactly that.
- Refusing declared supersets at parse is NOT the fix: the commissioned refuse case needs the final panel to inherit `refuse`.

Removal controls (record each in the commit message, restored after the observed failure): (i) `emits` narrowing review-panel to its required results again fails the new case by name; (ii) `emits` widening unanimous-pass to the step's declared results fails `a_final_panel_that_cannot_emit_refuse_lets_an_earlier_refuse_end_the_sequence` by name.

KEEP: every check refuses by default; derived fields never serialized; no runtime vocabulary comparison; no witness or policy pin moved; no contracts/, fixtures/, policy/ or reference/ change; engine.rs and bundle.rs not grown; files under their ceilings; no suppression; no baseline raised; the public API at 2010 entries (name any change as an ask).

GATES:
- cargo fmt --all -- --check
- cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings
- cargo test -p brokkr-core --locked (timeout 280)
- cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --lib --locked (timeout 280; split by filter, `bundle::` and `engine::` first, if it cannot finish)
- cargo test -p brokkr-runtime --test it --locked -- crucible_review_sequence table_lints witness_digests:: frozen_contracts:: (timeout 280)
- cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it --locked -- decisions_index:: doc_truth:: suppressions:: frozen witness (timeout 280)
- cargo run --locked -p brokkr-cli -- compile --bundle recipes/self, and the same for recipes/verify
- typos --hidden; quality/ratchet.sh files, clones and api; git diff --check
- TMPDIR stays OUTSIDE this worktree (use /var/tmp, created in the same command if missing). Before reporting, `git status --short` shows no untracked file.
- Run every command in the foreground and wait for it. Never end your turn with a background job pending: this seat is non-interactive.
- A seat whose commands run through the `workspace` tool has a 300-second response limit per call, and a call that outlasts it leaves its command running and blocks the calls behind it, including the write of your result file. Wrap every command in `timeout 280` there, split a long suite by test filter, and if a gate still cannot finish inside the limit, report it UNVERIFIED (the controller's host coverage runs every test) rather than retrying it. Write your result file before any optional extra check.
- Commit when done, signed off (`git commit -s`), "engine: …" ending "(#429)", with the line "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>" LAST, directly after the sign-off with no blank line between. Record each removal control in the commit message. Never push. Do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh; the controller runs it.

ASKS TO NAME (for the PR, which opens as a DRAFT): the story's (a) `ends_on` derived and never serialized; (b) the hard vocabulary: every arm hard, and its destination stops the run by the engine's own `stops_run`; (c) the early-end payload's `step` and `why`; (d) no shipped table exempted; (e) witness pins and policy digests (expected: none moved); (f) brokkr-runtime's public API 2006 → 2010, and no brokkr-core line; (f-bis) `Aggregate::emits` as a documented vocabulary; (g) the follow-up: whether `review_panel` should turn an out-of-vocabulary member word into `__member-schema-invalid__` as `unanimous_pass` does (an aggregate output change, the operator's); and any new one.

SIZE (an estimate): about +10 to +30 production lines and +60 to +120 test lines.

KNOWN FLAKES, not this branch's: capability_broker tests and `machine_proof::` runs failing "MCP server box filesystem identity is not protected: admission did not complete before its startup deadline" under host load; brokkr-runtime engine::broker admission tests ending `Identity(Expired)` under load; brokkr-runtime engine::capability_tests::provision_tests (a timing bound, and writers_tests' EffectIndeterminate) under load; two brokkr-runtime engine "work chief commits" tests and heap_costs' one-byte compare difference under load; brokkr-protocol `oneshot::tests::a_produced_attempt_carries_its_result_and_checkpoints` (#932). If verify fails on one of these alone, the implement visit reruns it on the host alone (`-- --exact`, with HOME set), quotes both results, makes no commit, and reports COMPLETE, not blocked.

CONTENTION (NEVER message the-forge-9d or any brokkr-wt-* seat):
- Decision 0065 slice two's U9b1b and U9b1c (another session) are in brokkr-runtime capabilities and broker test files, bundle/mcp.rs, brokkr-cli verbs/setup.rs and broker/rpc*, and may touch brokkr-protocol adapters.rs; don't edit those.
- #908 (PR #934) is in brokkr-runtime places.rs, bundle.rs's `bound_input` and `Held::intact`, and bundle/walk.rs; leave them.

Every review position, panel member or chief, is READ-ONLY: it changes no tracked file and makes no commit. For a scratch, use `git worktree add` or `git archive HEAD | tar -x` into /var/tmp, never a byte copy of this worktree. It reports each finding, written as a test case: the bundle or table set up, the steps reported, and the ending observed against the ending expected.

# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.
